subject: Security exhibit — defining audit windows, pen-test access, and SOC 2 evidence cadence
messages:
From: Mike Harrington <mike.harrington@atlashealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>; karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Health Legal <legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit questions and pen-test window request

Diego / Karthik,

Thanks for the redlines over the weekend. We reviewed the MSA + security exhibit and have a few open items we need to close before procurement signs the order form: 

1) Pen-test access window — we need to agree on a 7-day window where our third-party vendor (SecureCheck LLC) can run a penetration test against the environment. Please confirm whether Redwood will provide a read-only support account and whether there will be an in-house contact during the test.

2) Audit rights language — your team’s last draft limits audits to SOC 2-related scope. Our legal team is asking for explicit language that allows a one-time on-site or remote audit per rolling 12 months with 30 days’ notice. We understand you may propose an alternative.

3) Evidence cadence — we typically collect SOC 2 reports + operational evidence quarterly for our internal compliance committee. Can you confirm expected cadence and what you can provide (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, exception logs, pen-test summaries)?

Attached: atlas_redlines_v2.docx (our redlines).

Can we aim to lock this by EOD Wednesday so procurement can route the Order Form?

Thanks,
Mike Harrington
Director, IT Risk & Compliance
Atlas Health

Attachments: atlas_redlines_v2.docx (docx, 147 KB)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Harrington <mike.harrington@atlashealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions and pen-test window request

Mike — thanks for the clear write-up and the redlines. Stamped a few notes inline (see attached) but want to propose a practical path to close fast:

- Pen-test window: Redwood can offer a dedicated 5-business-day window with a designated support liaison on-call. For higher risk scans (active exploit attempts) we prefer a brief (<=48h) scoped window. Can you confirm whether SecureCheck will run authenticated tests (with credentials) or black-box? That determines what we can expose.

- Audit rights: we can accept a once-per-12-month audit, remote or on-site, with 30 days’ notice, provided audit scope is limited to SOC 2 controls and production tenant-level data is not re-exported. We propose a short appendix that enumerates what is and is not in scope.

- Evidence cadence: Redwood publishes SOC 2 Type II annually; operational evidence (change logs, access reviews, exception reports) can be shared quarterly via our secure evidence portal. For pen-test summaries we can share redacted reports and remediation attestations within 10 business days of completion.

Next steps: I’ve looped in Karthik (legal) to formalize the proposed exhibit language and Marissa (CS) to confirm scheduling logistics with your vendor. If that works, we’ll produce a one-page exhibit supplement and attach to the Order Form via DocuSign.

Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Diego@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0186

Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions and pen-test window request

Mike / Diego / Marissa,

I looked through Atlas’s redlines and Diego’s proposed carve-outs. Below are the legal edits I recommend for the security exhibit. I attach a plain-text draft for ease of collaboration (security-exhibit-proposed-legal.txt). Key items: 

1) Audit scope — language: “Customer may, once in any rolling 12-month period and upon providing not less than thirty (30) days’ prior written notice, conduct an audit of Redwood’s controls solely to the extent necessary to validate Redwood’s compliance with the SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria applicable to the Services. Such audit shall be conducted remotely unless otherwise agreed in writing, and Customer shall not export or take custody of Customer data beyond what is required for the audit.” (I removed broad 'on-site' rights without prior agreement.)

2) Penetration testing — language: “Customer’s third-party testing vendor may perform penetration tests against the Customer’s provisioned environment during a mutually-scheduled 5 business day window. Tests that attempt to exploit production data or that require elevated system-level access must be pre-approved in writing. Redwood will provide a single technical point-of-contact during the testing window. Redwood will not provide privileged/support accounts that create persistent elevated access.”

3) Evidence cadence — we will commit to provide SOC 2 Type II report (annual) and a quarterly evidence bundle consisting of: change log summaries, access-review attestations, exception reports, and pen-test executive summaries (redacted). We will reference our secure evidence portal link instead of attaching raw logs.

If Atlas requires broader access (e.g., on-site extraction), we will ask for a separate SOW and expenses. Also recommend adding a mutual non-disruption clause: tests shall be conducted to avoid material service degradation and Redwood reserves the right to pause tests that cause service-impacting behavior.

Please confirm if Atlas legal will accept remote-only as the default and the 5-business-day window. If yes, I’ll produce the tracked exhibit and send it back for a final run.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Mike — appreciate the quick review and patience. Confirming we can proceed on the path below and our proposed timeline: 

- Legal language: Redwood accepts remote-first audit rights once per 12 months with 30 days’ notice. Karthik will send the tracked exhibit by EOD today.
- Pen-test window: 5 business days (SecureCheck to confirm black-box vs authenticated). Please provide SecureCheck scope and credentials requirement by Wednesday so we can pre-authorize any authenticated tests.
- Evidence cadence: SOC 2 Type II (annual) + quarterly evidence bundles via our portal. We will send a short onboarding link to Atlas’s compliance mailbox after countersignature.

Next steps:
1) Karthik to attach the tracked exhibit (will do today).
2) Mike / Atlas to confirm SecureCheck scope and preferred dates.
3) Marissa to add the exhibit to the Order Form and route via DocuSign once Atlas confirms.

DocuSign link for the current Order Form: https://secure.docusign.com/Redwood/AH-2026-0421 (please confirm once you receive it).
